title: Composable invoker: stabilize parallel fan-out, deterministic result injection, and OpenAI-compat adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Stabilizes multi-tool fan-out and result injection with new invoker flags; introduces an OpenAI-compatible adapter for function-call ordering and streaming handshake. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in ergonomics for advanced flows.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see production signals (internal canaries + two customer incidents) where complex multi-tool call graphs produce non-deterministic result ordering, intermittent duplicate injections, and streaming handshake mismatches with OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR consolidates several workstreams into a single composable invoker surface that: (1) makes parallel fan-out stable across retries and preemption, (2) enforces deterministic result injection ordering onto response streams and structured output payloads, and (3) provides an OpenAI-compat adapter that preserves function-call ordering and streaming handshake semantics for downstream SDKs and third-party connectors.

Summary of changes: - Introduced Invoker orchestrator (invoker/composable) that coordinates child tool runners using a pluggable scheduler (round-robin, affinity, sequential). The default scheduler is affinity-aware and best-effort deterministic. - New invocation options: injection_mode ("ordered" | "unordered"), prefer_parallel (true|false), max_concurrency (int), idempotency_key (string). These flags are surfaced on the API layer and in the internal invocation context. - Deterministic injection pipeline: results from parallel runners are collected into a sequence buffer with configurable commit semantics (first-commit-wins, last-success-wins, sequence-order). The default is sequence-order to match prompt/tool declaration order. - Retry contract: retry metadata (attempt_id, causal_chain_id) added to tool results to deduplicate injections and allow idempotent retries. We also add a lightweight local cache to short-circuit duplicate tool runs within a single top-level request. - OpenAI-compat adapter: translation layer that maps function-call semantics to Redwood tool calls while retaining streaming partials and function-call name/args ordering. Adapter includes a short handshake for streaming clients to ensure the first function call start event is not reordered with partial content. - Structured output enforcement: schema hints are attached to tool outputs and merged deterministically. When schema validation fails, a structured failure object with error_code and canonical_reason is injected instead of raw text. - Observability: new metrics (invoker.fanout.concurrency, invoker.injection.latency, invoker.duplicate_injections, invoker.retry_rate) and a per-request trace span for the invoker orchestration. - Tests and stability: added unit, integration, and a deterministic e2e test harness that simulates timing jitter and worker preemption. Also added a small perf canary that runs on the perf-lab nightly suite.

Commit summary: - c3f9a2e: Introduce invoker/composable orchestrator and interfaces - a2b7ea1: Implement affinity scheduler and ordered buffer commit semantics - f08d4b2: Add retry metadata and idempotency short-circuit cache - 9d1b6c8: OpenAI-compat adapter and streaming handshake implementation - ba7c9e4: Schema enforcement and structured failure objects - e5f9c1a: Tests: unit + deterministic e2e harness + perf canary config - 6a2b4d5: Docs: API option surface and migration guide

Files changed (high level): - invoker/composable/* (new): core orchestrator, scheduler implementations, buffer/commit primitives, metrics hooks - api/handlers/invoke_api.go: surface new invocation options and validation - adapters/openai/*: adapter layer translating OpenAI function-call/streaming to internal invoker semantics - runtime/runner/*: small runner-side changes to emit retry metadata and accept idempotency keys - tests/e2e/invoker_jitter_test.go: deterministic harness with orchestrated jitter - docs/api/invoker.md: migration and examples - perf/canaries/invoker-fanout.yaml: nightly canary job

Code snippets / usage examples (illustrative): - API-level flag example: {"tools": ["lookup","translate"], "injection_mode": "ordered", "prefer_parallel": true, "max_concurrency": 4, "idempotency_key": "req-20260228-xyz"} - OpenAI-compat example: client receives function_call events in the same order tools were declared; partial streaming chunks are prefixed with handshake=invoker-v1 to avoid reordering spikes.

Design decisions and alternatives considered: - Defaulting to sequence-order injection preserves the principle of least surprise for users who expect tool outputs to appear in prompt-declared order. We considered first-commit-wins (faster) but it led to subtle non-determinism during retries and preemption. - Affinity scheduler gives better locality for heavy-weight tools (GPU-backed) and lowers KV-cache churn compared to pure round-robin. - We chose to implement the OpenAI adapter as a thin translation layer so that downstream SDKs do not need to opt into Redwood-specific flags; adapter is opt-in per-route.

Backward compatibility and migration: - Backwards-compatible by default: if no invocation flags are provided, invoker falls back to legacy behavior (best-effort unordered injection). - To opt into deterministic injection and the adapter, customers set injection_mode and enable the openai_adapter route flag. - No changes to persisted data formats; retry metadata is included only in response headers and internal traces.

Testing, CI and perf: - CI: full unit and integration suite ran; one flaky test (runner/worker_pool_test) was adjusted to use the new jitter harness and re-ran green. - Perf: local perf runs show 2-6% tail-latency increase for ordered injection under high contention; however, expected token-cost reduction due to deduped retries for idempotent flows. - Observability: dashboards added under invoker -> fanout; alert set for invoker.duplicate_injections > 1% for 5m.

Review conversation (high-level): - Diego: requested clearer semantics on idempotency keys and how they surface to the API; added explicit validation and docs. - Priya: asked for a failure mode where schema enforcement could obscure useful raw output; added structured failure object that includes original raw output as an optional field (masked for PII). - Owen: requested tracing spans include tool-level timing and causal_chain_id; added span instrumentation and updated the trace schema. - Author replies: addressed comments, added tests for idempotency short-circuit, and clarified migration steps in docs.

CI and merge status: - All CI checks green on the final run: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e jitter harness (pass), perf-canary (scheduled). - PR reviewed and approved by reviewers above. Merged via squash on 2026-03-03.

Open questions / follow-ups: - Rollout plan: feature gated behind route flag; recommend three-stage rollout (internal, beta customers, general availability). - Runtime optimization: consider a lightweight speculative commit (speculative-commit window) to reduce perceived latency for ordered flows; tracked in ENG-5199. - UX: add SDK convenience wrappers in python/ts SDKs to surface idempotency_key generation and openai_adapter enablement (follow-up PRs planned).

References and related work: - ENG-5123: invoker composability spike - ENG-5199: ordered-commit and speculative-commit proposals - SUP-8432: customer incident summary (non-deterministic tool ordering)

Checklist: - [x] Add invoker orchestrator and scheduler primitives - [x] Implement ordered buffer commit and retry metadata - [x] Add OpenAI-compat adapter and streaming handshake - [x] Add schema enforcement and structured failures - [x] Add metrics and traces - [x] Add unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Docs and migration guide added

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the new invoker surface backwards-compatible while providing explicit opt-in flags for production teams that need deterministic behavior. We should monitor invoker.duplicate_injections closely during the rollout and iterate on speculative-commit heuristics to improve latency/throughput trade-offs.
notes: Merged after reviewers sign-off and CI green. Opt-in route flag for initial rollout. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-5199 and SDK wrapper PRs.
